scope: Proposition 6.5 (Boundary arch estimate) of the manuscript “Gaussian free-field limits of weighted integer Lipschitz heights” (preprints/Gaussian-free-field-limits-of-weighted-integer-Lipschitz-heights-October-6-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 232 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 3dae0156982e5d20), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 57. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: There are constants L > 100, c, C > 0 and a positive slope tolerance such that the following holds. Fix p ∈ ∂D and a local radius R satisfying that tolerance. Suppose the actual prescribed trace on S0,δ is at least −1 everywhere and at least zero in QR(p) \ Qr(p). Choose any N positive scales 16r ≤ ℓ1, Lℓj ≤ ℓj+1, ℓN ≤ R/10. At all sufficiently small meshes, P  a site circuit in b O0(H) surrounds Qr(p) and is contained in QR(p) \ Qr(p)  ≥ 1 − Ce−cN . (6.9) The constants are independent of N, p and the prescribed trace; the required mesh threshold may depend on the chosen positive scales and the boundary approximation. The same assertion holds with all inequalities reversed when the original trace is at most 1 everywhere and at most zero in the clean annulus. All usable sites of the resulting arch have their real height at least zero, or at most zero in the reversed assertion.
